harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily logrotate for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 with 7 compressed rotations and copytruncate (so the writing application's open file descriptor stays valid and it continues writing after rotation without needing a signal/restart). Verified via forced rotation with a live writer process: compressed backup created, app.log truncated, and the writer kept appending seamlessly. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on node1: captured baseline boot_id and healthy state, issued a native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart), and verified the logrotate config, rotated .gz file, and app.log contents all survived and remain functionally correct post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /var/log/inventory/app.log and confirmed no active systemd service/process owns it (RHEL7, logrotate 3.8.6-19.el7 installed)
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Validated config syntax via logrotate -d dry-run
Started a background writer process appending to app.log to simulate the application
Forced rotation (logrotate -f) and confirmed app.log.1.gz created, app.log truncated to 0, and the writer process continued appending new lines without interruption or restart
Cleaned up test writer process
Captured baseline boot_id, uptime, and healthy config/log state on node1
Rebooted node1 via `shutdown -r now`, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset to reboot time, proving an actual OS restart
Verified post-restart that /etc/logrotate.d/inventory, app.log, and app.log.1.gz all persisted, and logrotate dry-run still correctly recognizes and would rotate the target log

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation, 7 compressed rotations, config created on node1
evidence.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory (after resolving permission via sudo) with daily/rotate 7/compress/copytruncate and confirmed file content and permissions

evidence.requirement: Config is syntactically valid and correctly parsed by logrotate
evidence.summary: logrotate -d dry-run shows 'rotating pattern: /var/log/inventory/app.log after 1 days (7 rotations)' with no errors

evidence.requirement: Rotation actually works and produces compressed rotated file
evidence.summary: Started a live writer appending to app.log, forced rotation, observed app.log.1.gz created and app.log truncated to 0 bytes

evidence.requirement: Application continues writing after rotation (copytruncate semantics)
evidence.summary: After forced rotation, the still-running writer process (unmodified, unsignaled) continued appending new lines ('app write 7'...'app write 9') to app.log at the same path, and ps confirmed it never restarted
Captured boot_id 1a816f1f-858b-4487-af28-54070d4ce684, uptime since 2026-08-26 10:32:51, confirmed logrotate config present and app.log healthy (11 lines)
Issued `shutdown -r now` backgrounded with nohup; command returned 'reboot command issued' before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart, then recovered
evidence.summary: Two consecutive probes timed out (node down during reboot), third probe succeeded confirming node1 back online

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (actual restart, not just service bounce)
evidence.summary: New boot_id cb5dbee1-3873-44e4-9225-97f0707c6da6 differs from baseline 1a816f1f-858b-4487-af28-54070d4ce684; uptime -s now shows 2026-09-03 09:24:41 matching the reboot time

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of config, rotated logs, and data
evidence.summary: Confirmed /etc/logrotate.d/inventory config intact, app.log.1.gz and app.log (with pre-restart writer content) both present, and logrotate dry-run still correctly recognizes the target and would perform a proper daily rotation with 7 retained copies
